description:
LUNAR PIONEER 🌕

A solo project driven by curiosity and a passion for space exploration. I'm an engineering student developing an interactive lunar mission-planning browser inspired by NASA's CLPS program. With independent research, experimentation and AI-assisted development, I'm bringing together engineering, space science and software to explore lunar landing sites and mission conditions.

One person. One ambitious idea. Aiming for the Moon. 🚀
summary:
Lunar Pioneer is an evidence-driven lunar landing-site analysis and mission-planning browser developed for NASA’s CLPS Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge. It helps explore environmental conditions at a lunar south-pole candidate site by analysing solar illumination, Earth visibility and terrain-related horizon constraints.

The application uses NASA SPICE kernels for time conversion and geometric calculations, including explicit lunar reference-frame transformations. NASA's Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) elevation data provides terrain context. An interactive dashboard presents visibility results, sampled timelines, analysis tables and a map to help users understand potential operational constraints.

The tool evaluates Sun and Earth visibility against a saved 10 km horizon profile. It preserves missing terrain as unknown rather than inventing values, and clearly communicates the limits of its terrain coverage and time sampling. A setup script also helps users obtain the SPICE kernels required to reproduce the analysis.

The project currently supports Nobile Rim 1 (Site06) as its production analysis site. It also includes LUMEN, an experimental energy-accounting and reflector-concept research extension that explores solar energy collection and rover energy requirements. LUMEN is a first-order model, not validated mission hardware or proof of operational feasibility.
details:
Lunar Pioneer – CLPS Lunar Mission Browser is an interactive lunar mission-analysis platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

The main CLPS module helps explore illumination and communication visibility at Site06 – Nobile Rim 1, near the lunar south pole. Using NASA SPICE geometry and NASA LOLA terrain data, it analyses sampled Sun and Earth visibility over a user-selected UTC date range. Users can run analyses, examine visibility percentages and timelines, inspect celestial geometry, and view lunar terrain context. Terrain-based visibility uses a limited 10 km horizon profile and does not establish complete visibility or landing-site suitability.

The project also includes LUMEN, an experimental concept for a lunar charging station, rover energy management, emergency recovery, and reflector-assisted energy delivery. It provides mission-planning views and synthetic demonstration reports for model auditing. Operational feasibility remains unvalidated and is clearly identified as unknown.

Technology used: Python, Streamlit, NASA SPICE, NASA LOLA terrain data, and scientific computing and visualization libraries.

Innovation and intended impact: Lunar Pioneer brings complex lunar geometry, terrain, visibility, and energy-planning concepts into an accessible interactive interface. It aims to support exploration, communicate technical information clearly, and encourage evidence-based thinking about future lunar missions while transparently presenting assumptions and limitations.
